composition.story: Two centroids start at guessed spots among six points. Each iteration has two moves: every point joins its nearest centroid, then each centroid jumps to the mean of its points. Watch the centroids move far at first, then stop once assignments stop changing.

aha.observation: Each centroid moves to the mean of its points; once no point switches clusters, the mean equals the centroid, so movement is zero and k-means has converged.

states.label: Start
states.sentence: Both centroids begin at guessed positions; no point belongs to a cluster yet.
states.why: K-means needs starting centroids before it can assign anything.

states.label: Assign 1
states.sentence: Each point joins its nearest centroid: a, b, c go to A; d, e, f, g go to B.
states.why: Centroids have not moved yet; only point memberships change.

states.label: Update 1
states.sentence: Each centroid jumps to the mean of its points: A to (1.33, 2.00), B to (4.75, 4.75).
states.why: The mean is the position minimizing squared distance to that cluster's points.

states.label: Assign 2
states.sentence: Reassigning with the new centroids, every point picks the same cluster as before.
states.why: If memberships are unchanged, the next mean will equal the current centroid.

states.label: Update 2: converged
states.sentence: The means equal the current centroids, so neither centroid moves. K-means has converged.
states.why: Same members give the same mean, so the loop reaches a fixed point and stops.
